text:
maya (ml infra): heads-up, bringing up a new community model for eval: harbor-7b. license file attached in the repo but it looks like a hybrid clause (NC + attribution + no-weights-redistrib). can we ship quantized weights to dedicated customers?

alex (applied ml): quick context — baseline evals look fine, quantization at 4-bit causes ~1.8% drop on SQuAD-like pass@1 but otherwise ok. customers want an on-prem docker image with model baked in.

samir (legal): @maya thanks — share the exact license text? if it's NonCommercial (NC) then commercial hosting or selling would be disallowed. "No redistribution of weights" is pretty clear: we can't hand out the weights even if quantized.

maya (ml infra): pasted snippet: "Permission: use for research and non-commercial purposes. Redistribution of model weights prohibited. Attribution required in product UI."

samir (legal): ok that matches what you said. options: 1) host the model behind our API/edge and serve but not ship weights, 2) negotiate a separate commercial license with upstream, or 3) provide an enterprise-only hosted offering where we run the model in their VPC but still don't transfer weights.

liz (platform): technical note — option 3 (customer VPC hosting) is doable with Private deployment; we can do a managed instance where the weights stay in our infra and we never publish them to the customer. need to flag billing/legal, though.

alex (applied ml): follow-up: for evals we want to run quantized experiments and commit artifacts to our internal registry. are we allowed to store quantized checkpoints internally for internal evaluations?

samir (legal): storing for internal evaluation is generally ok under research/non-commercial clauses, but keep it limited — documented access control, audit logs, and keep it off public repos. we should add a record in the model registry marking `redistribution_permitted: no` and `commercial_use: denied` so downstream teams don't accidentally ship.

maya (ml infra): adding that right now. also question: can we publish evaluation logs or outputs (prompts/responses) derived from the model? the license says attribution required but doesn't forbid publishing outputs.

samir (legal): publishing outputs is usually fine unless the model's license says otherwise or the training data has restrictions. include attribution in the README or evaluation notebook. avoid publishing raw training data or anything that seems like proprietary content.

alex (applied ml): noted. one more wrinkle — some customers asked if we can provide a small plugin that downloads a quantized runtime and performs conversion client-side. would that violate "no redistribution of weights" even if the conversion runs locally?

samir (legal): yes, moving weights to customers in any transformed format is redistribution. Converting on their machine after we hand them a base checkpoint is distribution. If you keep conversion code public but weights remain server-side, that's fine.

maya (ml infra): ok, so path forward: do evals internally, keep quantized checkpoints behind access control, don't ship any weights. offer Private deployment or Hosted API for customers needing on-prem-like performance. legal to draft recommended registry flags and a one-pager for sales.

liz (platform): i'll add a flag to the model registry UI: `access_policy: "no-redistribute, private-hosting-only, attribution-required"` and a brief tooltip.

samir (legal): i'll write a short note for sales and solutions describing what we can offer vs what we'd need to negotiate with upstream (e.g., buyout or commercial license). cc @compliance-bot for record.

compliance-bot: logged: model harbor-7b added to compliance queue. ticket #C-7621. assigned to samir and maya.

alex (applied ml): thanks all. i'll proceed with 4-bit evals internally and open a PR that includes the eval metrics + the registry flags. will also add a checklist: `ensure_no_weights_export` before any customer deliverable. :white_check_mark:

maya (ml infra): perfect. tagging this thread in the onboarding runbook. :thumbsup:
